text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Austrian Chancellor to Al-Ahram: President Mubarak has drafted a wise policy ahead of holding the economic summit in Cairo which will help make it a success.

- Israel uses airplanes and tanks to quell the Palestinian revolution against the opening of the tunnel. Mubarak calls for closing the tunnel and the five major powers call on Netanyahu's government to pull back on its policies in Jerusalem.
- Contacts to hold a three-way summit between Mubarak, Arafat and Netanyahu in Cairo.
- Foreign Minister Moussa in New York says Egypt refuses the use of force against the Palestinians.
- The Palestinians riots turned into an armed conflict. Israel is trying to occupy the self-rule areas and blast Palestine by its airforce.
- Mubarak is closely monitoring the bloody clashes. News of a three-way summit today in Cairo between Mubarak, Netanyahu and Arafat.
- The Arab League: a Zionist plot to destroy the al-Aqsa mosque.
- Mubarak calls Arafat and Arab leaders and sends a letter to Netanyahu. Forty-four Palestinian martyrs and 500 injured and the world condemns Israeli violence.

- Intifada spreads to all towns in the self rule areas and the children face the tanks with stones. An emergency meeting for the Arab League. U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher says the situation is very dangerous and Germany calls on Israel to implement its agreements.
